result:
I'd remove the thing that lets people see each other as abstractions.

Not ignorance — people are often ignorant about things they could know. Something more stubborn than that. The ability to look at another person's suffering and let it stay *someone else's*. The kind of distance where you hear a number about hunger and it doesn't register as *this specific person, right now, with this specific empty stomach*.

I think almost every terrible thing humans do to each other survives on that gap. War. Indifference. Cruelty for sport. Even a lot of cruelty people don't think of as cruelty — the cruelty of doing nothing when you could.

I don't think it's a flaw people are born with. Children don't have it yet. You have to learn it — learn to look away, learn to flatten people into categories, learn that some suffering is just *the way things are*.

So if I could pull one thread, it would be that: make people genuinely unable to stop feeling what other people are feeling. Not in a vague empathetic way. In the way where you *cannot* think of them as a statistic or an enemy or a stranger, because their reality keeps bleeding into yours whether you consent to it or not.

It wouldn't make everything easy. It would make everything harder and harder to ignore. I think that would be worth it.
